## C01 - M Vertica, RM489,000 / 850 sf

Selected evidence E15; three bedrooms/two baths, partial furnishing. Tower, floor and parking unidentified. This is the principal counterexample to a blanket central-Cheras affordability objection.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | E39 spans multiple years and possibly primary transactions; small/large area anomalies remain. The RM690k project median is not a denominator for discount. Matched 850-sf sale leads justify investigation only. |
| G1 | City employment access plus ordinary daily retail/services can support use by working households. Existing MRT and Velocity are already operating anchors; no new-rail appreciation thesis. Tower-specific post-VP history matters. |
| G2 | Primary exit buyer: budget-conscious working couple/small household wanting three separate rooms near inner KL. Secondary: long-term rental investor. False borrowed buyer: premium integrated-Velocity owner who values a different address/interface. Same-weekend set: other actual 850-sf M Vertica units first, then compact Maluri alternatives; Aster/Maxim only if commuting task overlaps. |
| G3 | Family-capable room count counters a purely investor-only label. However 3,684 units concentrate near-substitutes. Need lift-zone loading, car-park journey, short-stay/partition controls and listings deduplicated by tower/type. Large total supply does not itself prove poor occupancy or governance. |
| G4 | Missing parking is materially important at this quantum; furnished-title conflict prevents condition premium. Reject road/rail-exposed stack only if intolerable impact is demonstrated for the target buyer, not merely from a map. |
| G5 | No validated mispricing. Strong relative research priority because three-bedroom quantum undercuts selected peripheral examples, not because the project must recover an old median. DF01 active. |
| G6 | Nominal break-even about RM522k; 8% illustrative equity hurdle needs RM592k. Future comp set includes ageing M Vertica resales and newer Velocity supply. Owner route plus investor route gives potential redundancy, but both can remain credit-sensitive. Long-term rental is a hold fallback, not a sale exit. |
| G7 | Base rent RM2,400 is unverified; cashflow about -RM2.0k/year. Single-property forced-hold leaves RM307k. Lease expiry/valuation and maintenance unknown; no title or financing pass. |
| G8 | Joint first research tier with C05. Stronger central access hypothesis versus C05's extra area/balcony. Do not buy both simply because each individually fits; combined stress breaches protected reserve. |
| G9 | **Defer - high investigation priority.** Upgrade only with clean exact-unit identity, competitive normalised clearing, acceptable management and observed tenant/buyer use. Downgrade if advertised price needs unavailable terms, actual parking is inadequate, or sustained competing offers remove resale room. |

## C02 - Shamelin Star, RM700,000 / 1,054 sf

E16 selected ask; four advertised rooms, two bathrooms, partly furnished. E06 supports project identity. This high-quantum expression is intentionally retained to challenge the temptation to reward a familiar neighbourhood automatically.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | Nine observed transactions do not establish clearing for this configuration. E33's 980-sf RM620k/RM640k leads require area, parking and condition reconciliation. |
| G1 | Local residential/work/service utility on the Shamelin side can be distinct from Maluri's integrated precinct. Paying RM700k needs a project/unit advantage, not proximity to the same malls. |
| G2 | Primary: local upgrading household with Shamelin/Pandan routines. Secondary: working-household rental investor. False borrowed: walking-MRT buyer or school-specific purchaser without verified route/admission needs. Same-weekend alternatives: smaller Shamelin Star, suitable mature Shamelin/Pandan condos, then C01 at lower quantum. |
| G3 | 630 units do not prove low operational density. Historical cooperative short-stay accounting prevents an owner-only assumption. Current governance/use composition must be established. |
| G4 | Four rooms may differ from approved bedrooms; sale/rental bath counts differ. Bay count absent. Require plan/light/ventilation and vehicle fit before attributing family value. |
| G5 | No supported discount. RM700k competes for a meaningfully different budget from C01/C05; neighbourhood attachment cannot explain away the extra capital. |
| G6 | Break-even RM780k; 8% hurdle RM886k. At that exit, larger and different-housing-form substitutes enter the buyer's search. Needed premium must come from demonstrated livability and buyer adoption. No numerical ceiling inferred from the 980-sf rows. |
| G7 | Assumed RM2,600 rent gives about -RM10.1k annual cashflow. Single shock reserve survives, but lease expiry and current major works remain open. |
| G8 | Low priority at this ask: more entry capital and carry than the first-tier cases without demonstrated compensating exit advantage. A cheaper smaller unit would be a new expression, not a retrospective pass for this one. |
| G9 | **Defer - price/fit, low priority.** No structural Reject warranted. Would move up for original practical bedrooms, sufficient parking and matched resale evidence supporting a substantially better price-to-utility relationship. |

## C03 - EkoCheras 762-sf one-bedroom duplex, RM520,000

E17 and E26. Freehold, furnished, one-bay indexed description. Analyse as a couple/single-person lifestyle product, not a three-bedroom family substitute.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | Broad EkoCheras transaction commentary combines Tower E flats and H/J duplexes. No mixed median or RM480k indexed ask is treated as cleared comparable. |
| G1 | Retail/rail convenience reduces daily friction for users who value it; internal stairs and mixed-use circulation narrow product fit. The area can be desirable while this layout suits only part of its buyer pool. |
| G2 | Primary: single professional/couple valuing the specific duplex experience. Secondary: conventional whole-unit rental investor. False borrowed: Mutiara landed family or family requiring three enclosed bedrooms. Same-weekend set: same tower/type duplex first; other genuine compact rail-linked residences second. |
| G3 | Verify residential access separation, lift use, short-stay rules/enforcement and resident traffic. Mall adjacency is a Driver for some users and a penalty for others. Neither direction is assumed for every unit. |
| G4 | Confirm mezzanine/upper area, headroom, stair use, usable furnishing space and bathroom/powder-room distinction. Gross 762 sf is not equivalent to 762 sf of single-level usable family space. |
| G5 | No mispricing claim. Affordable absolute quantum earns a niche place, but freehold cannot make an unsuitable layout a family asset. |
| G6 | Break-even RM561k; 8% hurdle RM635k. Future resale to a couple or rental investor must survive conventional tenancy economics. If income only works with short-stay operations, the thesis changes and exit redundancy weakens. |
| G7 | RM2,300 assumed long-term rent; about -RM4.5k/year. Freehold removes one tenure-expiry concern, not bank, management or building-age risk. |
| G8 | Specialist allocation, below C01/C05 for the broad household mandate. Could rise for a buyer explicitly prioritising car-light couple use; that is a mandate change, not universal superiority. |
| G9 | **Defer - niche expression.** Resolve unit and long-term rental economics. Reject only a demonstrated non-remediable fit/operational failure for the chosen investment buyer, not duplex form in general. |

## C04 - Aster Type B, RM540,000 / 810 sf

E18 refreshed; E08 official plan interpretation and user Red Team calibration inherited. Not scored as a new blind discovery.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | Aster aliases and geocoding remain dangerous; E45 wrongly places the apparent project near Cochrane. Potential 807-sf records need address/parcel reconciliation before any valuation. |
| G1 | Connaught rail access with daily local utility supports working households; campus demand is only one channel. Prior user observation establishes plausible family capability, not realised price premium. |
| G2 | Primary: compact family/working household needing separate rooms and rail access. Secondary: conventional investor. False borrowed: all UCSI students as future owners or all Cheras landed households. Same-weekend competitors: Type B, Maxim 1,050 sf and other comparable rail-access options. |
| G3 | Investment-oriented positioning does not erase family layouts. Need evidence of actual owner adoption, management, leasing turnover and same-type supply. |
| G4 | Prior official B plan: three bedrooms/two baths, no balcony drawn. Two bays claimed; their geometry and exact stack remain unknown. C-type's extra utility must be priced separately. |
| G5 | No validated discount. B has better investment entry priority than paying RM650k+ for C merely because C is more comfortable. DF04 carries the user-identified landed substitution conflict. |
| G6 | Break-even RM585k; 8% hurdle RM664k. At higher exit quantum, new/older larger condos and selected landed alternatives press harder. Need durable B-type ownership demand, not an assumption of appreciation into C pricing. |
| G7 | RM2,400 rent remains inherited assumption; about -RM4.3k/year. Lease expiry/title/financing unverified. Single shock leaves RM291k. |
| G8 | Next tier after C01/C05, subject to whether its actual station route and operational experience earn the smaller-area premium. Compare the same household's full travel and living task. |
| G9 | **Defer - conditional shortlist.** Prefer B's quantum for further investigation; do not reverse the earlier Red Team correction. A C-unit can overtake B only on incremental price, rent and proven exit willingness-to-pay together. |

## C05 - Maxim Residences, RM480,000 / 1,050 sf

E19, three beds/two baths, balcony/two bays claimed; normal sale advertisement, not the obviously erroneous RM123k index lead. Exact title/unit identity must distinguish other Maxim-branded developments.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | E38 has mixed sizes, motives and an unusually low 1,033-sf tail. No reason established for that tail; neither discard it as an anomaly nor price the entire project from it. Normalised price unresolved. |
| G1 | Practical space and lower quantum can satisfy local Len Seng/Connaught household demand. Investment mechanism is price-to-functional-utility, not generic Cheras growth. |
| G2 | Primary: local working family accepting this building/access to obtain more space. Secondary: whole-unit rental investor. False borrowed: Aster's exact linked-route buyer without route substitution test. Same-weekend set: same 1,050-sf stock, Aster B and suitable Connaught Avenue stock. |
| G3 | Verify lift/corridor/parking burden, condition, management collection and repair plan. An older occupied project must retain desirability as nearby newer stock ages into resale supply. |
| G4 | Balcony and two bays are meaningful hypotheses; actual area definition, usable layout and bay positions need verification. Source route inconsistencies make station benefit conditional. |
| G5 | No established discount. Lower selected total price, larger area and potential balcony support relative investigation priority; superiority fails if defects/access costs consume the apparent advantage. |
| G6 | Break-even RM516k; 8% hurdle RM587k. Family plus conventional investor are potential exits. Future competing rent offers and fresh Aster/Annex/other Connaught resale supply must be compared by actual housing task. |
| G7 | RM2,400 rent assumption; about -RM1.6k/year, least negative in this scenario set. Leasehold expiry, valuation gap and works remain open. Single shock leaves RM304k. |
| G8 | Joint first research tier with C01. Stronger space/quantum expression; weaker unverified access/condition tradeoff. No purchase on PSF alone. |
| G9 | **Defer - high investigation priority.** Require actual layout/condition, two enforceable usable bays and matched transactions explaining both normal range and low-tail sale. Drop priority if acceptable units require substantially higher entry or recurring expenses. |

## C06 - Riana South, RM595,000 / 947 sf

E20; furnished three-bedroom, two-bay ask at Bukit Mandarina/Alam Damai edge. Do not label the whole Alam Damai/Damai Perdana belt from this edge case.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | E37 gives close-size transaction leads, but duplicate rows, floor, parking and achieved terms are unresolved. RM595k being near reported RM603k is not enough to pass normalisation. |
| G1 | Education and local working-household demand may support rent. Quiet/green residential positioning needs actual daily access and unit observation; neither university presence nor developer name proves family resale preference. |
| G2 | Primary proposed exit: local owner household needing three bedrooms and two bays. Secondary: long-term investor serving legitimate household/student tenants. False borrowed: all university users converted into owner buyers. Same-weekend: same947 type, Maxim/Aster if routines overlap; larger Altitude 236 as a research comparator, not valued here. |
| G3 | Room-rental advertisements and altered-bedroom examples require separation from original family layouts. No inferred building-wide partition rate or management defect. DF02 tests whether rent strength translates to owner demand. |
| G4 | Furnished package quality, exact floor, daylight, unmodified bedrooms and traffic/noise need verification. Do not accept the phrase beside UCSI as a measured walk. |
| G5 | No mispricing. At RM595k, the investment must earn its premium over C05 through better achievable rent, operating performance or resale adoption. |
| G6 | Break-even RM639k; 8% hurdle RM725k. Future buyer must choose this 947-sf asset against larger/residential alternatives at that quantum. Investor exit weakens if rent growth depends on extra partition rooms. |
| G7 | RM2,700 assumed rent below visible whole-unit asks; about -RM4.2k/year. Credit/lease and operational documents remain gating. A whole-unit fallback is explicitly required. |
| G8 | Second tier. Potential rent support deserves verification, but the broad family thesis is less evidenced than attractive rent advertisements suggest. |
| G9 | **Defer - investigate rent/ownership divergence.** Upgrade for actual conventional tenancy receipts and independent owner-buyer comparables; downgrade if most income requires an operating model the future buyer will not accept. |

## C07 - Green Residence, RM540,000 / 1,127 sf

E21; Batu 9/Taman Rasa Sayang, three bedrooms/two baths, two bays, partial furnishing. Correctly assigned to the Suntex/Batu 9 side, not BTHO.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | E34 larger-unit transactions cannot be scaled linearly. Exact marketed parcel is not identified and photographs may be illustrative. No discount claim or appraisal from the RM450 project median. |
| G1 | Space, freehold tenure and residential environment may attract car-using local households. Station proximity is not sufficient to price as walkable TOD; hill/road access must be observed. |
| G2 | Primary: local family seeking a more residential product within this budget. Secondary: whole-unit investor, with weaker modelled yield. False borrowed: YOU City station-interface tenants transferred without friction. Same-weekend: same size/type first; appropriate YOU Residence/Vista and local family stock second. |
| G3 | Product positioning is promising but current operating quality unknown. No assumed Binastra/SDB quality transfer. Verify actual effective competitor supply and project-specific management. |
| G4 | Need exact tower/floor, slope-side/outward adjacency, bay access and authentic unit photographs. Two-car family suitability includes the drive from gate to road, not only two painted bays. |
| G5 | No mispricing. More area than Aster at the same ask does not necessarily compensate for poorer rental economics or access. |
| G6 | Break-even RM616k; 8% hurdle RM702k. Exit increasingly competes with larger condos and landed options. Family desirability needs to support quantum, not just a higher PSF opinion. |
| G7 | Assumed RM2,000 rent yields about -RM9.3k/year. Freehold does not remove funding/capex/valuation risk. Single-property shock remains fundable. |
| G8 | Better family-livability research candidate than a yield-first purchase at this ask. Preference falls behind C01/C05 under the fixed investment mandate; may rise for long own-use holding. |
| G9 | **Defer - price/income burden.** Upgrade for substantially better achieved whole-unit economics or an entry supported by true matched sales. Not rejected for car dependence alone. |

## C08 - Windows on the Park, RM900,000 / 2,497 sf

E22, large four-plus-one-bedroom, three-bay freehold expression. E40 gives unusually useful current governance evidence, but does not certify this unit. The small/medium layouts are separate research targets.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | Mixed-size project median is inappropriate: low PSF on a very large unit may simply price quantum. No demonstrated recoverable gap to normalised clearing. |
| G1 | A maintained landscape and shared services can support a distinct low-maintenance family lifestyle. Positive evidence earns research priority for the project, not any price for every size. |
| G2 | Primary: established family specifically choosing spacious strata living over a house. Secondary: larger-household tenant/investor, probably a narrower pool at required yield. False borrowed: every local landed upgrader. Same-weekend: same large Windows units and smaller layouts, with BTHO landed as diagnostic alternatives. |
| G3 | E40 improves the governance evidence base relative to unknown peers. Long-term tenancy is compatible with good community operation. Forthcoming works still require accounts/approved budgets; no unsafe-lift claim is made. |
| G4 | Three bays and usable single-level space could defend preference. Need genuine layout, floor/stack, actual maintenance share units and externalities. The RM850 fee allowance is not derived by multiplying RM3.58 by square feet. |
| G5 | No discount. DF03 examines low PSF versus high total capital requirement and competition. A governance advantage is not a free capitalisation premium. |
| G6 | Break-even RM1.029m; 8% hurdle RM1.173m. At those prices the target buyer must actively prefer the condo service package to local houses and other large residences. Large size may widen living utility while narrowing transaction depth. |
| G7 | Assumed RM3,500 rent is weakly evidenced; about -RM15.3k/year. Base forced-hold leaves RM155k, barely above RM150k reserve; zero-rent, valuation shortfall or higher levy breaches it. Positive management does not insure the investor's own balance sheet. |
| G8 | **Preserve Capacity:** near-exhaustion of mandate headroom with uncertain large-unit rent/exit, while lower-quantum alternatives remain. This is an allocation decision independent of unresolved G0, not a claim that the building structurally fails. |
| G9 | **Preserve Capacity for this RM900k expression.** Retain the project as a leading family-quality investigation, especially smaller/medium units. Reassess under a larger-capital or own-use mandate; never silently convert this result to a project-wide Reject. |

## C09 - Evergreen Park Scot Pine, RM498,000 / 1,743 sf

E23 preferred coherent advertisement, two bays and medium floor. The RM350k wrong-project lead E44 is excluded. Room layout and exact identity still require original documents.

| Gate | Application / decision implication |
|---|---|
| G0 | Three registered-price observations in a limited window and one visible close-size sale are too sparse to normalise this medium-floor unit. Alias coverage can distort apparent volume. RM498k is not certified undervaluation. |
| G1 | Local Sungai Long households and UTAR-linked accommodation are separate demand channels. Mature large-format stock can offer space at modest quantum; upkeep and operating intensity determine whether it remains a family substitute. |
| G2 | Primary proposed exit: budget-conscious local family wanting large space/two bays. Secondary: investor or parent purchasing legitimate campus accommodation. False borrowed: all UTAR students as permanent owners, or all Mahkota homeowners. Same-weekend: same Scot Pine type; genuine Cypress/Greenview/other appropriate stock only after identity and area adjustment. |
| G3 | Building age prompts capex investigation, not automatic rejection. Need MC collection, lifts, water systems, original room counts and tenancy/use rules. No assumption that student tenancy alone causes poor governance. |
| G4 | Advertised four-plus-one requires room/ventilation verification; refurbishment allowance RM40k may be insufficient. Parking access and particular block are needed. |
| G5 | Interesting low-quantum large-format lead; no validated discount. Would not pay RM550k just because it is a neighbouring ask while this coherent RM498k lead remains unexplained. |
| G6 | Break-even RM574k; 8% hurdle RM660k under RM2,200 assumed rent. At that future quantum, competing family products and houses matter. A rental-only investor exit becomes single-point exposure if family adoption is absent. |
| G7 | About -RM6.4k/year base cashflow; single stress leaves RM281k. A dedicated repair allowance is essential. Freehold cannot prevent liquidity loss or valuation/loan-tenure conservatism on deteriorating stock. |
| G8 | Specialist value/space investigation, after first-tier C01/C05. Can move up if actual whole-unit rent and management are materially better than assumptions; do not increase projected student income to rescue it. |
| G9 | **Defer - conditional value lead.** Resolve actual project identity, condition/works and family/investor exit motives. Record future outcomes separately; no backfilled success if the cheaper lead disappears. |

## Portfolio decision now

No Deploy and no current structural Reject are established. Eight Defer decisions have deliberately different research priorities; C08 is Preserve Capacity. This is not a neutral ranking: C01/C05 deserve the next unit-level effort; C02 at its selected ask and C08's large-unit expression do not. All 36 pairs fail the simultaneous reserve test. The next decision is to resolve high-value evidence for one candidate, not acquire several correlated properties to obtain nominal diversification.

## KV02 — Lavile Kuala Lumpur, 750 sqft (B01)

Catchment: Maluri–Cochrane. Advertised 2BR/2BA; bays: 1. Entry RM699,000; ordinary whole-unit rent scenario RM3,200/month. Fully furnished sale and rental asks; inventories not matched. Selection purpose: Premium compact urban rental; challenge rental premium versus acquisition quantum. Evidence: [E04](https://www.iproperty.com.my/property/cheras/lavile-kuala-lumpur/sale-502031924/), [E05](https://www.iproperty.com.my/property/cheras/lavile-kuala-lumpur/rent-501827333/), [E06](https://www.iproperty.com.my/property/cheras/lavile-kuala-lumpur/rent-107733488/).

| Gate | Evidence / conditional interpretation | Conclusion / unresolved burden |
|---|---|---|
| G0 — Reference-Price Validity | E04 is asking consideration, E05 is rental advertising/proxy, not a paired completed transaction. Other 750-sqft Lavile units are primary; EkoCheras duplex, M Vertica 850-sqft and Cochrane products are diagnostic total-budget/routine choices, not interchangeable rents or PSF. Premium furnishing needs explicit inventory matching. | STOP. Effective unit price, material comparability and justified clearing interval unvalidated. No discount claim. |
| G1 — Market Mechanism | Compact urban rental convenience may command a rent premium, but that premium must cover the much higher entry quantum and continuing fit-out burden. Existing retail/rail proximity is not fresh appreciation. | Mechanism hypothesis; no automatic catalyst, rent growth or appreciation credit. |
| G2 — Buyer Universe | Primary: working couple/single needing a separate study/guest room in the Maluri routine. Secondary: compact owner household. International-school or large-family demand is not transferable to 750 sqft by assertion. | Buyer tasks are analyst hypotheses, not observed proportions or additive independent pools. |
| G3 — Project Quality | Developer identity is available; current MC accounts, actual collected fees, lift/circulation conditions, occupancy and unique resale inventory are not. Rent listings do not establish an owner premium. | Operations/supply sufficiency not cleared. Unknown management is not assumed bad or good. |
| G4 — Unit Quality | One bay, actual usable area, privacy, neighbouring stacks and mixed-use circulation require inspection. Furnished sale does not prove equivalent quality to the rental lead. | Marketed expression only. No plan/condition/rights clearance. |
| G5 — Price / Mispricing | At assumed rent and fees: 5.49% gross; standard balance RM115/month. Mechanical 6% price: RM640,000. | G0–G4 prerequisites unresolved. Mechanical price is not fair value, a bid or proven mispricing. |
| G6 — Exit Architecture | Future small-household buyers must choose this unit over larger same-budget homes. An attractive tenant rent can coexist with weak owner willingness-to-pay; terminal price cannot be justified by a tenant's income alone. Five-year nominal break-even sale RM749,931; future standard buyer instalment RM2,988/month before fees. | Required sale is not forecast. Actual buyer cash/income, substitutes and sale time unproven. Flat/-20% exits and 12-month delay are modeled. |
| G7 — Financing / Terminal Risk | Do not assume property type labels settle land/title, tariffs, financing or remaining capital works. Higher price increases cash exposure even with a positive standard proxy. | Standard 90/4/35; separate actual-credit 15% valuation shortfall, 25-year loan, 5.5% rate and works/forced-hold sensitivities. No bank approval. |
| G8 — Portfolio / Opportunity Cost | Synthetic RM500k cash/RM150k reserve and correlated asset shocks; compare all opportunities against keeping capital available. | User capital, debts and real correlation unknown. Synthetic pass is not allocation approval. No assumed salary/refinance rescue. |
| G9 — Capital Decision | Upstream evidence, rights, costs and exit gaps remain material. | **Defer.** No independently proven structural failure justifies Reject; no demonstrated personal allocation constraint justifies Preserve Capacity. |

### Financial chain and sensitivity

Entry cash RM119,850; loan RM629,100; instalment RM2,785/month. Fee proxy RM300; other allowance RM250/month; initial works RM15,000. Eleven collected months produce annual carry RM-4,826. Year-5 debt RM583,453; flat-price whole-investment result RM-49,403; 20%-lower exit result RM-185,009. Taxes/unquoted transaction costs remain unverified, not assumed known zero.

Rent sensitivity RM3,000–RM3,400, plus fee +/-20%, is a stress grid, not an achieved-rent confidence interval. Standard coverage requires RM3,085/month; annual carry neutrality requires RM3,639/month under these cost/collection assumptions. Neither is a rent forecast. Exact financing and fee evidence can change the result.

### Four separate conclusions

- Product / living quality: conditional buyer-task fit described at G2/G4; comparative current operating quality is unverified. One bay, actual usable area, privacy, neighbouring stacks and mixed-use circulation require inspection.
- Investment attractiveness at stated price: 5.49% scenario gross yield and RM115 standard balance; negative annual carry, no validated G0 margin. No executable investment ranking.
- Research priority: Conditional standard surplus, below preferred 6% gross and negative annual carry. Investigate after the more affordable B01 compact case; no validated living-quality superiority.
- G9: **Defer**. Confidence is high that a Deploy is presently unsupported; confidence in fair value and actual performance is low.

Material divergence status: D04. Unresolved material conflict reduces conviction and increases the required evidence/margin; no numerical margin is invented when fair value itself is unbounded.

### At most three immediate evidence tasks

1. Verify same-package achieved rent and renewal.
2. Establish effective 750-sqft clearing evidence and competing larger homes at terminal budget.
3. Obtain fee/MC/works and exact-unit condition pack.

Routes: existing public developer/official/transaction records first; exact signed tenancy, fee/MC accounts, title and condition require a seller/management/lender/field diligence packet. No third-party outreach, paid access or site visit has been performed. Recheck before any rank promotion or offer. At the next active evidence pass, advance only if an available source can change the decision; otherwise retain Defer and the specific unresolved task, without repeatedly counting the same ad.

Work-queue disposition: advance decision-changing evidence investigation. Outcome status: no matured investment result; paper calculations and source-error detection are not hits.
